scope: Engine-light audio event identity, bus and snapshot state, typed parameter contracts, and spatial attachment intents that reference an anchor id, with a thin Unity AudioMixer adapter planned separately
review_note: The URLs below were not fetched from the authoring environment because its network egress policy blocks them; the admitted claims come from the author's prior reading of these documents and must be confirmed by a person before the admission record is signed.

sources.license_or_terms: Unity documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: The Unity Manual audio section is the engine's maintained primary audio documentation; version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Engine boundary: the source, listener, clip, and mixer objects that the adapter binds to and that the Core must not depend on
admitted_claims: Audio playback is modelled as sources in the scene heard by a listener, with clips as the played content
Sources can be routed to an AudioMixer group instead of directly to the output
Spatial blend, distance attenuation, and spatializer plug-ins are configured on the engine side per source
excluded_uses: Core does not reference AudioSource, AudioListener, AudioClip, or any other engine type
No claim about playback, DSP, or spatializer behavior without a compatibility profile and device evidence

sources.license_or_terms: Unity documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: AudioMixer is a shipped, maintained engine feature documented in the Unity Manual; version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Adapter boundary: mixer groups as buses, snapshots as mix states, and exposed parameters as the only script-settable values
admitted_claims: A mixer is a tree of groups with a master group at the root, and each group carries effects with parameters
Snapshots capture group and effect parameter values and can be transitioned to over a duration
Only parameters explicitly exposed by name can be set from script, and setting an unknown name reports failure through the return value
excluded_uses: No mixer asset, group layout, or effect chain is copied or prescribed
Core does not model effects, send levels, or the mixer's authoring window

sources.license_or_terms: Unity documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: The Audio Spatializer SDK page is part of the maintained Unity Manual; version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Evidence that spatialization is a per-source plug-in concern selected at the project level, which places it outside the Core and outside the adapter's validation claims
admitted_claims: A spatializer is a native audio plug-in selected in project settings and enabled per source
The spatializer receives the source and listener positions from the engine rather than from gameplay code
Distance attenuation and the spatializer's own processing are separate stages
excluded_uses: No spatializer plug-in is implemented, bundled, or selected by the family
No claim about spatialization quality, latency, or platform spatial-audio behavior

sources.license_or_terms: FMOD documentation terms; architecture facts only, no FMOD code, API, or content copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: FMOD Studio is a shipped, maintained, widely licensed middleware with versioned documentation; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Independent evidence that event identity, buses, snapshots, and typed parameters form the common kernel of a game audio system
admitted_claims: Events are the unit that gameplay triggers, identified separately from the audio assets they play
Buses form a routing hierarchy and snapshots override mixer property values as a whole state
Parameters have a declared type and range and are the contract between game code and the audio design
excluded_uses: No FMOD runtime, bank format, or API surface is wrapped or depended upon
No claim that the Core is compatible with any FMOD version

sources.license_or_terms: Audiokinetic documentation terms; architecture facts only, no Wwise code, API, or content copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: Wwise is a shipped, maintained, widely licensed middleware with versioned documentation; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Second independent evidence for event identity, bus routing, state and switch groups as closed mix state, and game parameters with ranges
admitted_claims: Events posted from game code are identified by name or id separately from the sound objects they act on
States describe global mix changes and switches select among closed alternatives, both distinct from continuous game parameters
Game parameters carry a declared range and are set per game object or globally
excluded_uses: No Wwise runtime, SoundBank format, or API surface is wrapped or depended upon
No claim that the Core is compatible with any Wwise version

sources.license_or_terms: Epic documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: MetaSounds is a shipped, maintained second-engine audio implementation; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Second-engine evidence that typed inputs with declared kinds separate gameplay from the sound graph and that the graph itself stays outside gameplay code
admitted_claims: A MetaSound exposes typed input parameters that gameplay sets by name
Triggers and continuous values are distinct input kinds
The sound graph is authored as an asset separate from the code that drives it
excluded_uses: No Unreal type, asset format, or graph node is copied
No claim about DSP or procedural sound generation in the family

sources.license_or_terms: Epic documentation terms; architecture facts only
sources.maintenance_evidence: Sound Classes and Sound Mixes are a shipped, maintained second-engine implementation; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Second-engine evidence that a bus hierarchy with inherited properties and named mix states is the common kernel of mix state
admitted_claims: Sound classes form a hierarchy in which child classes inherit property adjustments from parents
A sound mix applies a set of class adjustments as one state with fade in and fade out durations
Mix states can be pushed and popped rather than edited in place
excluded_uses: No Unreal type, asset format, or tool is copied
No claim that the Core reproduces Unreal mix modifier semantics

sources.license_or_terms: EBU publication terms; definition facts only, no measurement code copied
sources.maintenance_evidence: EBU R 128 is the maintained loudness normalization recommendation referenced by broadcast and streaming platforms; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: Evidence boundary: loudness is measured in defined units over a programme, so it is a measurement claim outside an EditMode test and outside the Core
admitted_claims: Loudness is normalized to a target programme level expressed in LUFS rather than by peak level
Loudness range and true peak are separate measurements from programme loudness
Measurement follows the ITU-R BS.1770 algorithm with gating
excluded_uses: No loudness meter, gating, or true-peak measurement is implemented by the family
No claim that a mix graph or a parameter contract makes output compliant with any loudness target

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, or platform authority
The first implementation is an identity, mix-state, parameter-contract, and attachment-intent substrate, not a playback engine, middleware bridge, or mixing tool
Spatialization, latency, loudness, and headset comfort are measurement and device claims that require a Device Lab receipt or a defined measurement procedure, never an EditMode result
